no municipal GIS publishing presence at all

— neither in the shared catalogue nor as their own ArcGIS Online organization. An ArcGIS Online search for each returned only false positives from elsewhere: Grimsby (UK, via Historic England), Pelham (Massachusetts), West Lincoln (Oregon), Thorold (historical map scans held by Brock University). Their websites resolve but serve no data.
Consequence: the Niagara side of the atlas will be internally asymmetric, the same way the Hamilton/Niagara split already is.

Niagara Falls and St. Catharines will have parcel-level authority; Wainfleet and West Lincoln will have OSM and the NEI only. This must be visible in the UI for the same reason the Hamilton gap must be — a reader seeing sparse coverage in Pelham would wrongly conclude Pelham has no industry.

This is the most methodologically useful find of the Welland pass, for two reasons.
It is a second, independent business register for one municipality.
businesses in Welland; the city's own directory records
. Two authoritative sources, same place, same rough period, disagreeing by ~29%. That disagreement is measurable, and measuring it tells us how much weight a register-versus-OSM gap actually deserves
we publish anything derived from one register alone.
It carries exact employee counts where the NEI carries bands.

(year established). Welland is therefore the one municipality where the NEI's bands can be calibrated against real counts — which matters directly for any floorspace-per-employee or parcel-area-per-employee underuse ratio.
Welland should be the engine's test municipality.
It is the only place in the region where a scoring output can be checked against two independent registers, exact employment figures, two epochs of zoning, and building footprints.

The western/Halton end of the study area is the weakest part of the whole source base, and it has not improved across three reconnaissance passes:

ArcGIS Online org has 8 public items, none industrial, and possibly refers to Burlington Vermont. No DCAT feed at any usual Hub path. The 403 suggests a portal that exists and refuses automated requests rather than one that is absent.
Consequence: Burlington is in the core scope and is covered by
the Hamilton nor the Niagara datasets. Any region-wide layer or score will be weakest exactly there, and it is the one hole that cannot currently be patched from an adjacent tier.
Next step is a human look at burlington.ca's open data page, and a first probe of Halton Region.
Materially simpler than the Hamilton side.
Every municipal dataset in this pass is Open Government Licence 2.0
, published per-municipality but following the same template:

OGL 2.0 (Niagara Region) · (Niagara Falls) · (Welland) · (Fort Erie)
        · (Lincoln) · (Niagara on the Lake) · (City of St. Catharines)
Brock University and a few catalogue-level datasets are CC-BY 4.0; two are under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. All are attribution-only and compatible with each other.
The share-alike problem remains OSM's alone.

A derived layer built only from OGL 2.0 municipal sources carries no copyleft obligation; the moment OSM geometry enters the same derived feature, ODbL share-alike is in play. This is an argument for keeping OSM-derived and municipal-derived signals separable in the scoring output rather than merged into a single opaque number.
What this changes for the engine
The register is no longer only the NEI.

authoritative registers of what land is for, and they disagree with each other and with OSM in informative ways. Zoned industrial + designated Employment + no OSM feature + no NEI business is a much stronger signal than any one of those alone.
Parcel geometry now exists for the two largest cities

across Niagara Falls and St. Catharines. The point-in-polygon test proposed as the alternative to the UK atlas's 60 m centroid radius is now available for roughly half the region's industrial land, and the parcel is the right denominator for any area-based underuse ratio.
Constraint layers exist and should subtract.

floodplain, Natural Heritage System, archaeological potential and MTO buffers all reduce what a site can become. The UK scoring engine has no equivalent — its signals only ever add opportunity or subtract for evidence of occupation. A Niagara engine needs a third category.
Physical change is observable in Niagara Falls independently of the NEI
via the 2010/2018 footprint pair. Where the two registers agree that something left, confidence is high; where they disagree, that disagreement is itself the finding.
Coverage must be a first-class UI concept, not a footnote.

twelve municipalities have no municipal data at all. Any score computed region-wide will be systematically better-evidenced in Niagara Falls and St. Catharines, and the confidence score has to carry that.
